Subject: Quick follow-up + jurisdiction questionnaire (recap from today)

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through DataSphere's latency and compliance needs. Quick recap and the asks I promised: 

- Objective: pick a hosting mode for the pilot (Hosted API in-region vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem) that satisfies EU jurisdiction & audit needs while keeping latency within your SLOs for EU users.
- Immediate asks from your team: confirmation on whether any EU data must remain in a single country (e.g., France/Germany), and whether any APAC users require local processing or can tolerate EU routing.

I attached a brief jurisdiction questionnaire to capture the specifics (redwood-jurisdiction-q-jv1.xlsx) — if you can fill the few country-level items it will help us narrow the recommended configuration. Also attached a one-pager that summarizes the tradeoffs at a glance.

Proposed next steps:
1) You fill and return the questionnaire by EOD Thu (Nov 5) if possible.
2) We schedule a 30–45m technical deep dive (Ben + Jonas) to walk deployment architecture and network flow based on your answers.
3) Marissa will outline pricing/POC options once we land the deployment choice.

If it helps, I can sketch how a Hosted EU instance looks (no cross-border egress by default), and when Dedicated or Private would be recommended.

Cheers —

Jonas —

Thanks, that was helpful. I started the questionnaire and have a couple clarifying questions before I finish: 

1) When you say "Hosted EU instance (no cross-border egress by default)", does that guarantee processing and storage exclusively within EU borders (and is it per-country or region-wide)? Our legal team is asking if data can move between eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for load/availability.

2) For Dedicated vs Private VPC: what are the differences with respect to control-plane metadata (e.g., request logs, model telemetry) — does Redwood's hosted control plane ever see request payloads for Hosted or Dedicated? Our legal/compliance folks will want clarity for GDPR and data processing agreements.

3) APAC: we have a small subset of users in Singapore. If we opt for Hosted EU, can we route APAC requests to EU without violating any residency requirement (they can tolerate slightly higher latency but we need explicit confirmation on where the tokens are processed).

Last: could you send SOC2 reports and the security questionnaire link so my InfoSec colleagues can start the review?

I cc'd Bryce who handles procurement — he'll want to understand timelines if we need Dedicated/Private.

Best,

Alice / Bryce —

Thanks for the questions. Below is a concise mapping to help your legal and engineering teams triage quickly. I'll attach the short security links and SOC2 pointer at the bottom.

1) Hosted (EU region-only)
   - Data storage and inference compute are provisioned in our EU region (we typically use a single cloud region such as eu-west-1 or eu-central-1).
   - Cross-region failover: by default we do not replicate customer inference payloads to another region. Replication for availability can be configured but requires explicit agreement and usually pushes you toward Dedicated/Private.
   - Control plane: metadata (billing, usage metrics) is stored in our control plane. For Hosted, request payloads are processed in-region and are not retained past retention windows unless you opt into advanced logging.

2) Dedicated capacity
   - Dedicated GPU pool in the chosen region. Higher control over autoscaling and isolation.
   - Control plane still coordinates scheduling; we provide options to reduce telemetry and increase retention controls. For strict legal requirements, customers often request a Private deployment.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem)
   - Private control plane with customer-managed network. Option to run inference entirely within your VPC or on-prem (no cross-border flows).
   - Full audit logs integration with your KMS/HSM and no shared tenancy. This is the strongest posture for EU-specific jurisdictional guarantees.

Tradeoffs to consider:
- Time to POC: Hosted EU = fastest (days to weeks). Dedicated = weeks (capacity provisioning, network setup). Private/on-prem = months (packaging, security review, on-prem ops).
- Cost: Private > Dedicated > Hosted (unit economics).
- Latency for APAC users: If you host in EU, APAC traffic will traverse to EU unless you add an APAC routing region or deploy a Private footprint closer to APAC. For a small APAC user base that can tolerate +80–200ms, Hosted EU is often acceptable.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- You return the attached questionnaire — it will flag any country-level constraints.
- Schedule a 45m tech deep-dive with Ben (solutions) and our infra engineer to show network flows and options.
- I'll send SOC2 link and the security questionnaire for InfoSec.

SOC2 report (read-only link): https://redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/soc2-readonly/2026
Security questionnaire (short): https://redwood-secure.example.com/questionnaire/DS-2026-47

If you want, Ben and I can sketch two concrete architectures during the deep dive: Hosted EU (no egress) and Private VPC with no control-plane payloads.

—Jonas
